items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: often thought about how Jelly Roll Morton must have felt when he brought a sad band to Cincinnati way back when

ctx.x: So when the night was finished, I told the leader of the band that I didn't like it and thought it was not fair for them to play that number when they knew it was one that I played and to play it before me. They didn't do it any more but the pianist got mad and never spoke to me again. And I'm still crying in my beer because of that, ha! ha!

There is no need to mention the names of the musicians I had in this group except Jack Starling my pianist for a long time and Cecily Forde the singer. All that I can say is that it was the saddest group I ever had. But I was hooked and often thought about how Jelly Roll Morton must have felt when he brought a sad band to Cincinnati way back when. The booking agency that had engaged me for the Ambassadeur had promised me more engagements before I opened in Odense, but they had let me drop like a hot iron.

We were supposed to do some numbers especially as an attraction for 20 minutes and after we did what we could the first night the manager came to me and asked me when was I going to do my dance number. The agency had told him that I played trumpet, sang and tap danced. The guy was very brought down when I told him that I was happy to be able to walk and didn't know one step in tap dancing.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I didn't know if this Mr. "Jelly Roll" as he called himself, had done all the things he said he had.

ctx.x: One day the word got round that a famous New Orleans pianist was in town and as it happened to be a night that we were not working, most of the musicians in town turned up at the place where this pianist was staying and he took charge of every pianist that was in the place. His name was "Jelly Roll" Morton and he was a real talker. He had a diamond in one tooth and when he wasn't playing piano, he was talking about what he had done, where he had been and what he was going to do. He didn't drink any of the bootleg…

At that time, there was no books on jazz and the musicians that played it, so I didn't know if this Mr. "Jelly Roll" as he called himself, had done all the things he said he had. He was a pimp, gambler, hobo and pianist, but he was not looking like a hobo then and he could play piano.

Some months after, "Jelly Roll" came back to Cincinnati with the orchestra of Fate Marable. Fate played piano also but he directed the band most of the time. I never knew who the musicians were in this orchestra, but me and everyone that heard them knew that we had heard one of the best jazz orchestras that had come to town in those days, and I always found a way to hear the bands that came along.
